az_whipper_wall.blurb: A small wall in the Stewart Pocket climbing zone outside Payson, facing west and holding shade for most of the day. The face leans past vertical, so expect steep, sustained pulling. Most of the thirteen lines are trad, with a handful of bolted routes and one boulder problem. The grades cluster around 5.11, with a few easier leads in the 5.8 to 5.10 range and a couple of 5.12s above them. The rock is granite. It is a good stop for strong climbers who want a quiet, shaded afternoon, though beginners will find little at their level.

az_pillow_wall.blurb: A trad-only wall at Paradise Forks, on the west flank of Sycamore Canyon's north fork, between Williams and Flagstaff. The canyon is columnar basalt with hard, solid rock and crack systems, and this is one of its more approachable walls thanks to a run of moderate leads. Thirteen routes span roughly 5.7 to 5.11, with the bulk split between 5.9 and 5.11. In summer the wall drops into shade by early afternoon, which makes it a comfortable pick in warm weather. Pine forest surrounds the rim, and the crowds stay light.

az_cattleguard_boulders.blurb: A cluster of boulders in Euro Dog Valley, part of the Queen Creek Canyon zone near Superior, set along a valley with a seasonal creek. The problems come in a range of heights and styles, with a tall smooth face on the west side as the standout feature. Grades are friendly: a few easy warm-ups, a big group at V2, and just a handful of V3 and V4 problems, so it suits newer boulderers and anyone looking to rack up mileage. Rock is welded tuff.

az_poor_decisions.blurb: A single large boulder perched on a ridge at the edge of the Icecapades boulder cove in the Phoenix area. Almost the whole block is climbable, giving thirteen problems from an easy V0 up to V7, with a cluster of harder ones around V5 and V6 and only a few in the V2 to V3 range. Most lines top out near thirteen feet, while the tallest, about twenty-five feet, is a high V5. The south face is the one pictured most often. The walk in follows the trail loop around the base of the first mountain, then finishes with a steep scramble of roughly two hundred feet.
